gap: No public benchmark evaluates retrieval over overlapping successive regulatory revisions with per-passage version labels and an in-force ground truth. Existing resources either score end answers on synthetic statutory questions (arxiv:2605.23497), measure gold-passage recall on Wikipedia/tennis versions (arxiv:2401.13222), or test temporal QA over non-versioned snippets (doi:10.1145/3589335.3651895).

evidence.quote: we present a benchmark of 312 expert-validated, time-sensitive German statutory QA pairs spanning three categories
recall@1 and recall@5 metrics, which compute the number of times the correct passage is in the top 1 or top 5 results
The TIQ benchmark contains 10,000 questions with ground-truth answers and underlying snippets as supporting evidence.

why_unaddressed: The retrieved benchmarks were designed for different units of analysis: Prior et al. label QA pairs by the version required to answer but evaluate only generated answers with an LLM judge and report no retrieval metrics, while TempRALM evaluates gold-passage recall in a Wikipedia setting without legal validity intervals. No retrieved work labels both retrieval candidates by version validity and queries by target date in a regulatory corpus.
research_question: Can a clause-level benchmark of overlapping regulatory revisions with version labels and in-force ground truth be constructed such that retrieval-layer version-selection accuracy can be measured separately from answer accuracy?
potential_experiment: Build a clause-level benchmark from amended statutes with archived version snapshots, per-version effective/expiry dates and time-stamped queries, and report version-selection accuracy@k (fraction of top-k passages from the in-force version) alongside end-answer accuracy, stratified by current versus historical query regime.
verification_required: A broader search of 2024-2026 legal-IR and temporal-retrieval venues for point-in-time or as-of-date statutory retrieval datasets is still required; the present search budget is exhausted and Semantic Scholar was intermittently unavailable, so the absence of such a benchmark is a bounded negative finding.
